bullets.title: MRVL +20-25%: Jensen calls it 'next trillion-dollar company' at Computex; CEO pitches connectivity bottleneck thesis
bullets.body: Marvell surged 20-25% premarket after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang highlighted MRVL as the 'next trillion-dollar company' at Computex. MRVL CEO Matt Murphy argued connectivity — not compute or memory — is the real AI infrastructure bottleneck, with copackaged optics (CPO) moving from proof-of-concept to mass production. JPM views MRVL as a full-stack AI data-center connectivity vendor with optical tracking to $600M+ FY27 revenue with '2-3x expansion potential in FY28.'

bullets.title: HPE +26-27%: Monster Q2 beat; AI Cloud & AI segment +123% y/y; FY26/27 guide raised dramatically
bullets.body: HPE reported Q2 revenue $10.68B vs. $9.78B consensus (+40% y/y beat of 9.2%), EPS $0.79 vs. $0.53, and GM 36.9% (+270bps vs. expectations). Cloud & AI segment +123% y/y; AI cumulative bookings reached $16.4B with backlog $5.9B and orders more than doubling. FY26 EPS guide raised to $3.35-3.45 (from $2.30-2.50); initial FY27 EPS growth guided +12-16%. Elliott Management appointed Chris Hsu to board. Loop Capital upgraded to Buy, PT $75 (from $23); JPM raised PT 84% to $68; MS raised PT to $71. Supply constraints — not demand — are the primary gating factor through 2027.

bullets.title: GOOGL -2.7%: $80B follow-on equity raise (including $10B Berkshire placement + $40B ATM) spooks market
bullets.body: Alphabet launched an $80B capital raise: $15B common stock, $15B mandatory convertible preferred, $10B private placement with Berkshire Hathaway at $351.81 Class A, and a $40B at-the-market program commencing Q3 2026. The raise signals AI capex is now constrained by market financing capacity rather than internal cash flow — 22V estimates 2027 capex could reach $300B+. GOOGL fell ~2.7-2.9% premarket; analyst note: Amazon's 2027 consensus capex is $228B for comparison.

bullets.title: CRWD: JPMorgan raises PT to $800 from $475, maintains Overweight; F1Q27 earnings preview bullish
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its CrowdStrike price target to $800 from $475 while maintaining Overweight. F1Q27 Street consensus sits at $1.363B revenue and $1.07 EPS; field checks are leaning positive with VARs bullish on FY27 growth. Key focus areas include Falcon Flex adoption, SGNL/Seraphic/Pangea acquisition integration, and Next-Gen SIEM acceleration. CRWD is also included in Anthropic's Project Glasswing/Quiltworks announcement.

bullets.title: AVGO: Tomahawk 6 nearly sold out; AI networking revenues to triple FY26, double again FY27 to $45B+
bullets.body: JPM's Computex deep-dive highlights Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 (3nm, 102.4Tbps) tracking 6-9 months ahead of NVIDIA and 12+ months ahead of MRVL and CSCO; the chip is nearly sold out for the next year. AVGO maintains ~70% share of cloud/hyperscale switching silicon and has a 2-year cadence competitive moat. Wolfe Research is hosting a post-earnings webcast on 6/4 at 8:30am ET.

bullets.title: CRDO: F4Q26 clean beat (+157% YoY revenue), FY27 guide raised to $2.44B; optical tracking $600M+
bullets.body: Credo Technology delivered a clean F4Q26 beat with revenue +157% YoY and gross margin 68.3%. JPM raised FY27 guidance to $2.44B revenue and $6.20 EPS; optical tracking to $600M+ FY27 with '2-3x expansion potential in FY28.' JPM raised PT by $20 to $250. CRDO was -4.4% premarket per SA pre-market note, suggesting initial sell-the-news reaction despite strong fundamentals.

bullets.title: NVDA: Vera Rubin in full production; supply constrained by HBM4 + CoWoS-L; BlueField-4 security collab with Akamai
bullets.body: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin is in full production but supply is constrained by HBM4 and CoWoS-L packaging availability; JPM estimates ~2M Vera CPU front-end units translating to ~10K VR200 NVL72 racks in 2026. Separately, NVDA and Akamai expanded security collaboration integrating Guardicore Segmentation into Vera BlueField-4 STX storage architecture for Zero Trust in AI factories. NVDA CEO confirmed supply is sufficient for CPU/GPU demand overall but acknowledged constraints.

bullets.title: META: Arete upgrades to Buy ($735 PT, 22% upside); Conversations conference June 3 key catalyst; teen safety expansion
bullets.body: Arete Research upgraded META to Buy from Neutral with a $735 PT implying 22% upside from $600.47. Mizuho previews the Meta Conversations 2026 conference (June 3) as key for WhatsApp/Business Messaging monetization and AI integration, noting channel checks show META is 'firing all guns on monetization' with SMB self-serve onboarding as the next major TAM driver. META also expanding teen account content controls (13+) globally across Instagram, Facebook, and Messenger.

bullets.title: SNOW: F1Q product revenue $1,334M (+34% YoY), beat consensus $1,268M; FY27 guide raised $180M to $5,840M
bullets.body: Snowflake's product revenue of $1,334M beat consensus by ~5%; FY27 guidance raised $180M to $5,840M (+31%), driven by Cortex Code. SNOW is also acquiring Natoma for governed agentic access and hosted a Platform Keynote event on June 2. Data/analytics stocks gained +14.8% for the week ended 5/29. Databricks is viewed as incremental competitive threat via Unity Catalog enhancements.

bullets.title: GNRC +9-10%: Hyperscaler supply agreement lands; analyst raises FY27E EPS to $11.20, sees $1B+ large-MW sales
bullets.body: Generac announced a global supply agreement with a leading hyperscale data center operator, validating its strategy as a strategic backup power supplier. An existing $600M notice-to-proceed from one hyperscale customer was announced in 1Q26; backlog exceeds $700M. Analyst raised FY27E EPS to $11.20 (from $9.90) on +16% sales growth and current estimates already incorporate $900M large-MW DC sales in 2027 as a conservative starting point.

bullets.title: EQIX: Citi Buy reaffirmed; AI inference inflection underway, fabric bookings +70% YoY, 20% total return target
bullets.body: Following NAREIT REITweek management meetings, Citi reaffirms Buy on EQIX with a $1,240 PT and ~20% total return. MRR growing double-digit in 4Q/1Q; 2Q normalized recurring revenue growth expected to expand 10-11%. Fabric bookings grew ~70% YoY with early near-tripling of high-bandwidth port connections; 110 AI on-ramps from top AI and neoclouds now on platform. Net debt leverage at ~3.8x EBITDA.

bullets.title: INTU -6.2%: Goldman Sachs downgrade hits software sector; broader SaaS names reversing sharply
bullets.body: Intuit fell 6.2% premarket following a Goldman Sachs downgrade. Broader software sector showed sharp reversals: TEAM -10.2%, OKTA -8.4%, HUBS -8.3%, NOW -6.2%, CRM -4.6%, ORCL -4.7%, and MSFT -3.2%. DA Davidson flags IGV's 45% rally since mid-April as leaving valuations implying 5-year forward EPS CAGR falling from 12% to 9%, recommending IGV put hedges with PANW/CRWD/ORCL reporting in the next 1.5 weeks as a catalyst.

bullets.title: CRM: DA Davidson bearish — 'share donor,' acquisitions increasingly desperate, Agentforce reacceleration at risk
bullets.body: DA Davidson calls CRM a 'share donor' that is 'increasingly desperate with acquisitions' and flags Agentforce reacceleration as at risk despite some traction. CRM also confirmed acquisition of Contentful (valued ~$1-1.5B). Separately, 22V notes IGV software at stretched valuations after 45% rally, with PANW/CRWD/ORCL (24% of IGV) reporting next 1.5 weeks as the key volatility catalyst.

bullets.title: MDB: Atlas revenue $512M (+29% YoY), modest beat vs. accelerating peers; data/analytics stocks +14.8% weekly
bullets.body: MongoDB reported revenue of $688M (+25% YoY), beating consensus of $664M, with Atlas at $512M (+29% YoY) showing steady but not accelerating growth compared to peers like SNOW. The broader data/analytics basket gained +14.8% for the week ended 5/29, +38.6% monthly, outperforming IGV but underperforming the S&P 500 YTD. Databricks is viewed as incremental competition to MDB via Unity Catalog Iceberg enhancements.

bullets.title: NFLX CEO: 12-14% revenue growth, ad tier doubling to ~$3B, AI as efficiency tool — not a content threat
bullets.body: Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos (at Prof G Markets) reaffirmed guidance for 12-14% annual revenue growth with ~31.5% margins. The ad-supported tier is expected to roughly double to ~$3B in revenue this year. Sarandos views YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram as attention competitors, not content rivals, and positions AI as a production efficiency tool rather than a creative replacement.

bullets.title: CIEN: Q2 earnings preview — +72.7% YTD, 15.6% implied move; JPM hosting post-earnings call 6/5
bullets.body: Ciena reports Q2 earnings with Street at $1.50B revenue (in-line with guidance), EPS $1.46, and non-GAAP GM 44.0%. The stock is +72.7% YTD vs. S&P +10.5% and has beaten revenue consensus 17 of past 20 quarters. Options imply ~15.6% move. JPM is hosting a post-earnings follow-up call on 6/5 at 10:30 AM ET.

bullets.title: SHOP: -4.9% in Canadian trading; JPM expert call with Platinum Partner on 6/8 covers agentic commerce strategy
bullets.body: Shopify fell 4.9% in Canadian morning trading. JPMorgan is hosting an expert call on June 8 with Zettler Digital (Shopify Platinum Partner, 400+ e-commerce brands) covering SMB/enterprise adoption cycles, Shopify Payments, Shop Campaigns, and Sidekick AI-commerce/agentic commerce strategy.

bullets.title: APP: Citi adds to 90-Day Catalyst Watch; eCommerce platform general availability by June 30 accelerates store growth
bullets.body: Citi adds AppLovin to its 90-day catalyst watch list ahead of its eCommerce platform moving from pilot/referral to general availability by June 30, 2026. APP is also increasing Axon marketing spending ahead of the launch, which is expected to accelerate store growth and revenue.

bullets.title: TLN: Receives regulatory clearances for $3.45B natural gas acquisition; 960MW nuclear-DC deal with Amazon highlighted
bullets.body: Talen Energy received regulatory clearances for its $3.45B acquisition of 2.6 GW natural gas generation from Energy Capital Partners (Lawrenceburg, Waterford, Darby plants). Separately, Talen's prior $650M sale of a 960MW nuclear data center campus to Amazon continues to be highlighted as a first-mover model attracting competition in nuclear-powered AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Semiconductor market WSTS forecast surges to $1.51T in 2026 (+90%); memory +250%, SK Hynix doubling capacity
bullets.body: WSTS raised its global semiconductor market forecast to $1.51T for 2026, up 90% and sharply above the prior $1.0T March estimate, driven by AI computing and extraordinary memory expansion (memory alone expected +250% to $800B+; logic +37%). SK Hynix plans to double wafer capacity over 5 years; Kioxia expects NAND shortage to persist through Q4 2027 and is seeking long-term hyperscaler supply agreements through 2029+. SK Group chairman expects AI-driven memory shortages through 2030.
